newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso ends firm, tracks U.S. long bond.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso ends firm, tracks U.S. long bond.

text.p: The Mexican peso closed firmer for the fourth day in a row on Thursday amid a market watching declines in U.S. long bond yields, traders said.

"U.S. consumer data was in line with forecasts, but it was enough to bring long bond yields down," a dealer said. "That led to a flow of dollars into the market, in a continuation of a recent trend." The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate ended 1.4 and 2.2 centavos firmer, respectively, at 7.7620/7.7650 and 7.7500/7.7550 per dollar.
U.S. 30-year Treasury bonds were up 27/32 to yield 6.56 percent when the foreign exchange market closed in Mexico.
Dealers said the peso also gained strength in a delayed reaction to strong domestic industrial output figures.
"The market ignored the industrial production figures for a while, but as they were very good dealers absorbed them and the peso rallied," another dealer said.
The Finance Ministry said Mexico's industrial production in June had risen by 9.9 percent from the same month in 1996.
This compares with an average rise of 8.3 percent forecast in a prior Reuters survey of Mexico City finance houses.
Same-day peso contracts had closed mid-morning 1.95 centavos firmer at 7.7560/7.7595 per dollar.
